items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen after dinner. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes seems to be enough to get most of the gain, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Try not to eat dinner too late, as sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners in the program. Only 12.5% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later, so you're already doing a good job with this.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You're averaging 10.1 hours of overnight fasting, which is a good habit to keep up. In the program, adding overnight fasting to coaching changed some numbers, but it's still not clear how it affects sugar levels in real people.
